facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old Caucasian man presented with septic shock and bilateral lower extremity soft-tissue wounds
Medical history includes alcohol use disorder and newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (hemoglobin A1c of 7.5%)
The patient had no history or findings suggestive of cirrhosis
Blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae
Microbiology showed positive string test
Organism showed resistance only to ampicillin
Initial MRI: Showed left mid-tibia osteomyelitis with an adjacent abscess and right third toe osteomyelitis
Abdominal Ultrasound: Revealed an 8.4 × 11 × 13 cm liver abscess
Bone Scan: Showed increased uptake in the right humerus and bilateral femurs
Follow-up MRI: Confirmed osteomyelitis in right humerus and bilateral femurs
Right femur biopsy: Demonstrated abscess formation
Patient presented with bilateral lower extremity soft-tissue wounds
